newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil giant names new chief after resignation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil giant names new chief after resignation.

text.p: Pan Wenent was named president of Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp on Thursday to replace Chen Kuo-young, who resigned amid public and political pressure after a spate of accidents.
Pan had been a Chinese Petroleum vice president in charge of the oil giant's overseas projects and explorations.
Chen resigned on Tuesday in the face of mounting pressure that surged on Monday after a gas explosion at the company's northern Taiwan refinery killed a worker and idled the plant.
Chinese Petroleum has been plagued in 1996 by about a dozen serious accidents, including fires, spills and explosions.
The accidents have caused costly shutdowns of refineries, oil ports and other facilities, and forced the oil company to pay more than US$40 million in compensation.
